note: Ground truth for the coneflower. Ranges were written by Claude from the sources listed plus tolerances Claude chose; some numbers are the owner's decisions. They were written after the first four builds had been measured with earlier scripts, so they are not blind. The bloom-end check and the tiers were added after the independent review, I had already seen the old p90 results (3 of 4 builds ended near week 32), so the new end window is not blind either. Checks marked advisory are reported but never fail the gate: they rest on one photo or on a leaf reading that a photograph cannot confirm. Plan review, 26 Nov 2026: the owner approved bloom to October with a thin tail, tolerances of 2 weeks on bloom start and midpoint with a month-level window for the end, the 90 percent week dropped, the winter check and the head ramp kept as gate checks. Age 0 is a plug (a small first-year seedling as bought in spring, or from winter-sown seed); the planner may start a bought-bigger plant at an older age. Clump rerun, 27 Nov 2026: the 12-head cap and the 9-to-12 ramp are replaced by the draft ranges above (heads at ages 2 and 3, a mature clump of about 40 heads as advisory, stems and spread as advisory); the owner approved the approach and still has to confirm the age 2 and 3 numbers. Ages 1 to 3 head ranges were reset on 27 Nov 2026 to the owner-approved silhouette plan, before the plan's build was scored.

visual: Leaf colour: photographs measure hue 69 to 70, saturation 0.53 to 0.57 (Minnesota Wildflowers and Illinois Wildflowers leaf photographs, same measuring method each time).
First-year leaf outline: pointed oval, about 2.3 times as long as wide, upright (owner's nursery photograph). Not the cut, lobed leaf of an older plant.
Head from the side: egg-shaped cone, tan with a dark ring at its base, rays hanging steeply (Ozark Edge close-up).

Head from above: short domed gray-green cone, rays broad (about a third as wide as long), drooping and overlapping at the base; the disk flowers open from the base up, forming a dark ring around the gray cone (owner's Wilson Bros photograph, 27 Nov 2026). An earlier note, narrow rays with gaps (Joshua Mayer photograph, Wikimedia Commons), disagrees; the model's rays were widened to match the broader photograph.

First-year juvenile (NRCS seedling guide, PDF page 25): about 6 in tall with 4 to 6 simple, elongated leaves held out and up at different angles, no stems or heads. Bloom the second year after seeding.
Winter: large dark seed heads on wiry stems, a low rosette of colored leaves, no dead leaves hanging on the stems.
